calls.head: A tough night ahead for Kaprizov
calls.body: At home, the Jets keep sending DeMelo and Samberg out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Scott Arniel has been picking a defense pair for the other team’s top line. Tonight the Wild’s first line is Ek, Kaprizov and Boldy.

calls.head: In close against from distance
calls.body: The Wild get in close, but the Jets mostly shoot from distance. Minnesota is near the top of the league for shots from in close, and Winnipeg is near the bottom. Shots from in close tend to be more dangerous, so expect the Wild to do more of their damage around the net.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Jets beat the Wild
paras: The Wild’s Calvin Pickard was back in an NHL net for the first time since Jan 8, 2026. The first period was a wild one. Cole Perfetti struck first for the Jets just under two minutes in, but Kirill Kaprizov tied it 1-1 for Minnesota midway through the period. Mark Scheifele put the Jets ahead 2-1 late in the period. Kaprizov struck again 44 seconds later to tie it 2-2, but that’s where Minnesota’s luck ran out. Perfetti scored his second of the night on the power play late in the second to put the Jets ahead 3-2. Kyle Connor made it 4-2 early in the third, and Cole Koepke stretched the lead to 5-2 late in the period. Scheifele finished with a goal and two assists.
Don’t let the score fool you: the chances were a lot closer than that. Stuart Skinner made 19 saves for the Jets. The Jets moved to 4-1-1, and the Wild dropped to 4-2-1.
